pool.what: compounds with no superconductivity record that Radar sends to Hurricane
pool.rule: within 50 meV/atom of the convex hull, a band gap of at most 1 eV, magnetic or not, 2 to 5 elements, up to 40 atoms in the cell, elements Hurricane's training data covers; the list holds the 591 that Radar sends to Hurricane, one per chemical system, except the 537 too far from Hurricane's training data for it to give a chance

range.from: its errors on parent compounds first reported after its training data end

check.about: of the compositions of new parent compounds in its time windows, the share given at least an even chance: of those that superconduct, and of those measured not to superconduct

novelty.about: each candidate's distance, in its model's standardized inputs, to the nearest material the model learned from; beyond the distance that separates 95% of the training materials from their nearest neighbour in another chemical system or parent compound, it lies outside the training data

caveat: Hurricane learned measured Tc from cuprates, iron-based, heavy-fermion compounds and other oxides in the NIMS SuperCon datasheet; it reads the composition only and gives the chance that a compound superconducts and its Tc if it does. Many of these compounds would need doping or pressure, and a candidate is a prediction until an experiment checks it

check.note: The authors describe the YbRhIn5 spacer as a normal metal in this thin-film stack. No standalone YbRhIn5 transition-temperature limit is assigned here. The passage does not specify an applied pressure. This observation does not exclude superconductivity in other crystal phases, doped compositions or pressure conditions, and is not a direct validation of the JARVIS structure.
check.cite: T. Asaba et al., Nat. Commun. 15, 3861 (2024)

check.note: The introduction cites prior work reporting no transition to 0.020 K. This is not a new temperature limit for every strained film. Applied pressure is unspecified in the passage; the statement does not exclude superconductivity in other phases, doping or pressure conditions.
check.cite: M. Shimozawa et al., Phys. Rev. B 86, 144526 (2012)
J. Y. Cho et al., Chem. Mater. 20, 6116 (2008)
check.note: The original paper reports antiferromagnetic order near 10 K. Methods give susceptibility 2–300 K at 0.1 T and heat capacity 0.35–70 K. The heat-capacity floor must not be assigned to resistivity or treated as an explicit no-superconductivity cutoff. This audit did not establish a superconductivity absence statement to 0.35 K. Superconductivity outcome remains unknown.

reliability.about: false alarms: the share of the held-out compounds with no superconductivity record that Radar sends to Hurricane which lie inside its training data and get at least an even chance; the compounds of this list are those same compounds, so a candidate with at least an even chance is one of them
reliability.cite: T. Konno et al., Phys. Rev. B 103, 014509 (2021)
reliability.dismissed_about: trained only on reports dated before a family was found and asked about that family's first five years

not_known.about: Hurricane gives no chance to a compound further from every training compound, in its standardized inputs, than the distance that separates 95% of the training compounds from their nearest neighbour in another parent compound; such compounds are not listed
